fields.note: The protected grounds, the Section 8 example, the advertising ban and the 180-day/2-year filing windows are all in the document. The statement that a landlord may still refuse for insufficient income, poor credit, an oversized family or a zoning-violating occupancy does not appear in this document. The $10,000 first-offense penalty also does not appear.

fields.quoted_span:
You may file a complaint with us for free within 180 days
of the date of the alleged violation.
fields.note: The 180-day DCR complaint and the 2-year Superior Court window are supported. The 'penalties up to $10,000 for a first offense' figure is not in the document.
The field is empty and the document states no effective date for the provision.

fields.quoted_span:
The Division on Civil Rights enforces the New Jersey
Law Against Discrimination.
fields.note: The document describes the LAD as currently enforced, which is consistent with in_force. It is a 2015 brochure and has no explicit statement of current status.

fields.quoted_span:
The provisions of the LAD apply to the sale or rental of all
property including open land, whether for business or
residential purposes, with the following exceptions:
fields.note: The listed exceptions (owner-occupied two-family unit, room rental in an owner-occupied one-family home, same-religion preference by religious organizations, familial-status exemption for older persons) match the document. The single-sex residence exception is not in D068, but it appears in D067 per the coverage evidence.
